title: Sky retains a minority allocation of each Star's token supply, giving its USDS capitalization a venture-equity character
content:
Osero's tokenomics (A.2.8.2.6.2.1) set a total supply of 1,000,000,000 OSERO, allocate 677,777,778 to the Osero Prime Treasury (its SubProxy) of which 150,000,000 is earmarked for incentives, and record that "Sky retains 322,222,222 OSERO tokens, distributing these as specified in a future iteration of the Atlas." Skybase's Accord carries the same two subdocuments — Prime Treasury allocation and "Sky Retained Tokens And Reward Pools" (A.2.8.2.7.2.1.2.1, .2.2) — with the amounts deferred.

The recurrence of the *slot* across Accords, independent of the numbers, is what makes this structural. Sky's relationship with a Star is not a grant and not a loan: Sky supplies USDS Genesis Capital and holds a retained share of the Star's token, so upside from the Star's success flows back to Sky holders rather than only to the Star's treasury.

Two unresolved consequences follow. First, the retained tokens' distribution is deferred in every case, so the mechanism by which that upside reaches SKY holders is undefined at the time the capital leaves. Second, retained tokens are voting power as well as value — a Star that later establishes independent governance does so with roughly a third of its supply held by Sky, which complicates any claim that the Star is governance-independent.
description: Of OSERO's 1,000,000,000 supply Sky retains 322,222,222 against 677,777,778 to the Star treasury; Skybase's equivalent split is deferred, showing retained-token allocation is a standing Accord term.
